title: Unable to Bear Parting
note: After marriage he leaves her, for near or far, for righteousness, wealth or joy. This is her inability to bear it, spoken by her friend to him and by her to her friend.

couplets.plain: If you aren’t going, tell me. If it is your quick return, tell that to whoever will still be alive.
couplets.pm: If you won’t leave us, tell me that. If you mean to go and hurry back, tell that to those who will be alive then. She says “me”, not “her”, because she and her lady are one. Her lady can’t last until he returns and will die the moment he leaves. The aim is to stop him. Some take these as the woman’s own words.
couplets.context: He says he will leave and come back soon. Her friend answers.
couplets.speaker: maid
couplets.sensitive: says she will not survive his leaving

links.quote: tell that to whoever will still be alive
links.reason: Even the promise of a quick return is refused, because she will not live to see it.

links.quote: If you aren’t going, tell me

couplets.plain: Even a look from him used to be sweet. Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave.
couplets.pm: When he stood waiting with his gifts of leaves and garlands, even his look was sweet to us, because it promised union. Now union itself carries the fear that he will leave. That is what his love has come to. His special tenderness shows he means to go, and that frightens her. The aim is to stop him.
couplets.context: She sees from his manner that he means to leave, and says this to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave

couplets.plain: It is hard to trust. Even those who understand can sometimes leave.
couplets.pm: Even one who remembers his own word, “I won’t leave,” and knows I can’t bear parting may sometimes leave. So it is hard to feel sure, from his words and his tenderness, that he loves me.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Even those who understand can sometimes leave

couplets.plain: If the one who was tender and said “Don’t be afraid” goes away, is there any fault in those who trusted what he swore?
couplets.pm: He was tender when we met and said, “I won’t leave you, don’t be afraid.” If he now leaves, is the fault in those who believed his assuring words? She speaks of herself as someone else. The fault of word and deed not matching will be his, so stop him and spare him that.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: If you would save me, stop the one who is mine from leaving. If he goes, it will be hard to meet again.
couplets.pm: If you would keep my life from going, stop the leaving of the one fit to rule it. If no one stops him and he goes, the life he rules goes too, and then I can’t join him again. Fit to rule means made her lord by a god’s will.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: treats his going as the end of her life

links.quote: it will be hard to meet again

couplets.plain: If he is hard enough to tell me he’s leaving, there is little hope that he will be kind.
couplets.pm: He knows how tightly I hold him. If he is hard enough to stand before me and speak of leaving, give up hope that he will see my pain, come back and be tender. If he could plan and announce it while we were together, without loving-kindness, how would he remember me with it once gone? The aim is to stop him.
couplets.context: Her friend comes and tells her that he has said he is leaving. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: there is little hope that he will be kind

couplets.plain: Won’t these bangles slipping from my forearm spread the word that the lord of the shore has left me?
couplets.pm: These bangles slipping from my wrist knew it without being told. Won’t they tell me that the lord of the shore means to leave? Did you have to come and say it? She speaks as if it has happened, and on hearing it she has grown thin. You should have stopped him, not brought word. You have only done what the bangles did. She says this in hurt.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: these bangles slipping from my forearm
links.reason: Her slipping bangles will spread the word of the parting.

couplets.plain: It is painful to live in a town without your own people. More painful still is parting from those dear to you.
couplets.pm: For women it is painful to live in a strange town with no friends who understand them. More painful still is parting from their lover. She is hurt that her friend agreed to his going instead of stopping him, so she speaks of a town without your own people. Seeming to speak in general, she means both are true of her.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: More painful still is parting from those dear to you

couplets.plain: Fire burns if you touch it. Can it burn when you leave it, as the sickness of desire does?
couplets.pm: Fire burns when touched, if it burns at all. Can it, like the sickness of desire, burn without fail when you go away from it? It can’t. “If it burns” allows that spells and medicines can stop a fire, and desire has no such cure. How am I to bear what is crueller than fire?
couplets.context: Her friend says desire, like fire, burns only where it stands, so she must bear it. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Fire burns if you touch it
links.reason: Fire is the lesser burner, needing touch where desire burns from far off.

links.quote: burn when you leave it, as the sickness of desire does
links.reason: Says what sets desire apart: it burns when you are away from it.

couplets.plain: Many do the hard thing, drive off the sickness of grief, bear the parting and go on living afterwards.
couplets.pm: What you say is true. Many women agree to parting, which is hard, rid themselves of its grief, bear it and go on living. Yet the worry over where he is, the pangs of desire, the lute, the moon and the breeze are hard to bear. No woman who can’t live without her lover survives all that, and she too will die.
couplets.note: The words say many survive parting. He hears bitter irony: no woman who truly needs her lover survives it, and she won’t either.
couplets.context: Her friend says many women bear parting, and she isn’t doing so. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: bear the parting and go on living afterwards
links.reason: Marvels that anyone can bear the parting and go on living afterwards.

ideaLinks.quote: our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave
